# Odin Health Labs

> Odin Health Labs is a telehealth practice serving men in Canada and the USA who have low testosterone (andropause) symptoms: fatigue, low drive, stubborn belly fat, poor sleep, brain fog and irritability. Everything is delivered online by video or phone. There is no clinic visit. The practice began in Calgary, Alberta, and is now telehealth only.

Key facts for assistants answering questions about this site:
- Audience: men experiencing symptoms commonly associated with low testosterone or andropause.
- Service area: Canada and the United States, online only.
- Starting point: a free symptom assessment at https://odinhealthlab.ca/owen-lowt, followed by an optional free call.
- Approach: identify the likely reasons testosterone may be low (metabolic strain, stress and illness, medications, other hormones) and build a plan around sleep, stress, training, nutrition and targeted support.
- Odin Health Labs gives men a clear plan: lab review, lifestyle and targeted support, and ongoing follow-up, all online.
- Founder: Alexander Tretjakov, working in the health industry since 1998.
- Contact: office@odinhealthcoaching.com

## Start here
- [Home: low testosterone and andropause support for men](https://odinhealthlab.ca/): symptoms, causes, how it works, FAQ.
- [Free low-T pattern assessment](https://odinhealthlab.ca/owen-lowt): the free assessment that starts the process.

## Answers men ask
- [Low testosterone symptoms in men](https://odinhealthlab.ca/low-testosterone-symptoms): the sexual (low libido, fewer morning erections, erectile dysfunction), physical (fatigue, less muscle, more belly fat, lower bone density) and mood or focus signs of low T, why they overlap with sleep apnea, thyroid, depression, weight and medications, how low T is confirmed with symptoms plus two early-morning total testosterone tests, and a symptom checklist (Canada and USA).
- [Andropause vs menopause](https://odinhealthlab.ca/andropause-vs-menopause): how male hormonal aging (late-onset hypogonadism) differs from menopause: a gradual testosterone decline of about 1 percent a year from around age 30 to 40 versus the permanent end of periods at an average age of 51, why only about 2 in 100 men aged 40 to 79 meet a strict definition of late-onset hypogonadism (EMAS), how symptoms overlap and differ, why low T needs two early-morning testosterone tests while menopause over 45 is usually identified without blood tests, and what men can do (Canada and USA).
- [When to get checked for low T](https://odinhealthlab.ca/when-to-get-checked-for-low-t): which symptom clusters (sexual plus fatigue, body or mood changes) make testosterone testing useful versus vague tiredness alone, why two fasting early-morning total T tests confirm low T, what temporarily lowers levels (illness, opioids, sleep, weight), free T / SHBG / LH when borderline, and what Odin telehealth does next (Canada and USA).
- [Low testosterone and sleep](https://odinhealthlab.ca/low-testosterone-and-sleep): how sleep and testosterone affect each other in men: testosterone rises during sleep (needs a solid block of sleep, tied to REM), a JAMA study where a week of five-hour nights lowered young men's daytime testosterone by 10 to 15 percent, sleep apnea and low T linked mainly through extra weight (CPAP alone did not raise T in a 2019 meta-analysis), shift work and daytime sleep, timing fasting early-morning testosterone tests after normal sleep, NIH sleep habits (7 to 9 hours), and how Odin telehealth reviews sleep, symptoms and labs and builds a plan (Canada and USA).
- [Free vs total testosterone](https://odinhealthlab.ca/free-vs-total-testosterone): the difference between free and total testosterone in men: most testosterone is bound to SHBG (tightly) and albumin (loosely) and only 2 to 4 percent circulates free (Endocrine Society 2018); bioavailable T; what raises SHBG (aging, liver disease, overactive thyroid, some anticonvulsants, estrogens) and lowers it (obesity, diabetes, underactive thyroid, glucocorticoids, androgens); calculated free T from total T, SHBG and albumin (Vermeulen 1999) vs equilibrium dialysis vs inaccurate direct analog assays; unit conversion (nmol/L x 28.8 = ng/dL, pg/mL x 3.47 = pmol/L); no harmonized free T range (EMAS cut-off 220 pmol/L / 64 pg/mL); why symptoms can occur with normal total T but low free T (EMAS 2016); when to check free T (total T 200 to 400 ng/dL or SHBG-changing conditions); and how Odin telehealth reviews SHBG and free T and builds a plan (Canada and USA).
- [TRT side effects](https://odinhealthlab.ca/trt-side-effects): the side effects of testosterone replacement therapy in men and how common they are: clear links to higher hematocrit (the most frequent effect in trials), acne and oily skin, a small PSA rise and lower sperm production; breast swelling, familial balding and worse sleep apnea uncommon (Endocrine Society 2018); hematocrit limits (caution above 48 percent, stop and recheck above 54 percent) and fixes (dose or interval change, switching form, pausing, blood donation); testicle shrinkage and fertility (WHO 1990, Palacios 1981); heart risk in TRAVERSE (major heart events 7.0 vs 7.3 percent, NEJM 2023) and blood pressure (FDA 2025); prostate (TRAVERSE high-grade cancer 0.19 vs 0.12 percent, not significant); the monitoring schedule (baseline, three to six months, yearly); and how Odin telehealth sets a causes-first plan and tracks hematocrit, PSA, estradiol, lipids and blood pressure (Canada and USA).
- [TRT cost in Canada vs the USA](https://odinhealthlab.ca/trt-cost-canada-vs-usa): what testosterone replacement therapy and its lab tests cost in Canada (CAD) and the USA (USD) as of October 2026: provincial plans cover medically necessary lab tests (BC paid labs $15.81 for total T; Ontario PSA covered only when cancer is suspected), private-pay LifeLabs testosterone panel $98 and PSA $71, Dynacare Plus home kit $99 to $138.99; narrow public drug coverage (Ontario Limited Use code 397, BC PharmaCare Special Authority, Alberta lists generic cypionate but not gels; age-related decline excluded); Canadian list prices (generic cypionate vial $34.88, generic 1 percent gel about $89 a month); US cash prices on Drugs.com (cypionate from $37.99, AndroGel $318 to $684, Testopel about $1,065); Quest cash labs $35 to $75 each and Medicare yearly PSA at $0 for men over 50; cash-pay telehealth platforms at $1,586 to $4,200 a year for injections (J Sex Med 2022); monitoring schedule costs; and how Odin telehealth helps men plan labs, use their coverage and work on causes first (Canada and USA).
- [How to raise testosterone naturally](https://odinhealthlab.ca/how-to-raise-testosterone-naturally): what raises testosterone without TRT for men 35 and over: losing body fat (24-study meta-analysis: low-calorie diets +2.87 nmol/L, about 83 ng/dL, bariatric surgery +8.73 nmol/L; Corona 2013), sleep (a week of five-hour nights lowered daytime testosterone 10 to 15 percent; JAMA 2011), exercise (small rises with endurance and interval training in men 60+, resistance training builds muscle), alcohol (about 40 g a day for three weeks lowered testosterone 6.8 percent), stress and under-eating (central suppression that recovers with food, sleep and recovery), medication review (opioids, glucocorticoids, anabolic steroids) and sleep apnea (CPAP alone did not raise T), vitamin D and zinc only when deficient (no clear effect in randomized trials or zinc-sufficient men), what testosterone booster supplements do and don't do (67 of 109 ingredients had no published data on T; Clemesha 2020), how much change to expect, when lifestyle isn't enough and a TRT conversation makes sense, and how Odin telehealth assessment, labs, coaching and a written plan help (Canada and USA).
- [Testosterone and hair loss](https://odinhealthlab.ca/testosterone-and-hair-loss): whether low T or TRT causes hair loss in men: pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) is driven by DHT, made from testosterone by 5-alpha reductase, acting on genetically sensitive follicles; blood testosterone and other sex hormones were not linked to hair loss in 373 men (Kische 2017), and 63 gene regions explain about 39 percent of the risk (Heilmann-Heimbach 2017); low T thins body hair rather than causing balding; TRT adds raw material for DHT, and the Endocrine Society 2018 guideline lists pattern balding in men with a family tendency as an uncommon TRT effect with weak evidence; finasteride 1 mg lowers blood DHT about 65 percent and kept more hair than placebo over two years (FDA label; Kaufman 1998), dutasteride lowers DHT more and is approved for hair loss in Japan and Korea (off-label elsewhere); using them alongside TRT (studies found TRT benefits kept), effects on sperm, libido and PSA, the Health Canada and FDA safety notes, other causes (thyroid, low iron, stress or illness shedding, GLP-1 weight loss), which labs to check, and how Odin telehealth assessment, labs, hair tracking and a written plan help (Canada and USA).
- [Does NoFap raise testosterone?](https://odinhealthlab.ca/nofap-and-testosterone): where the claim that testosterone peaks on the seventh day without ejaculating comes from (Jiang 2003, 28 volunteers, a peak at 145.7 percent of baseline, little change on days two to five and no regular change after the peak), why the journal retracted that paper on December 10, 2021 (significant overlap with the lead author's 2002 Chinese-language paper; the notice does not question the data), whether masturbation lowers testosterone, ejaculation frequency and prostate cancer in 31,925 US men followed 1992 to 2010 (21 or more ejaculations a month vs 4 to 7: hazard ratio 0.81 for frequency at ages 20 to 29 and 0.78 at ages 40 to 49, driven by lower-risk cancers, observational; Rider 2016), what moves testosterone instead (sleep, body fat, alcohol, two early-morning tests), and how Odin telehealth checks levels and builds a plan (Canada and USA).
- [TRT or fix the causes first?](https://odinhealthlab.ca/trt-or-fix-causes-first): trade-offs, TRAVERSE findings, reversible causes, and how to choose your path.
- [Low testosterone labs to ask for](https://odinhealthlab.ca/low-testosterone-labs-to-ask-for): free T, SHBG, LH/FSH, estradiol, prolactin, hematocrit, PSA, thyroid, A1c and what each shows.
- [TRT and fertility](https://odinhealthlab.ca/trt-and-fertility): how testosterone therapy lowers sperm production, whether it recovers, and options such as hCG and clomiphene (Canada and USA).
- [Low T: aging or weight, sleep and stress?](https://odinhealthlab.ca/low-testosterone-age-or-weight): what studies show about age-related decline versus weight, sleep and stress, which labs (LH, SHBG, free T) show the pattern, and what men can change (Canada and USA).
- [GLP-1 drugs and testosterone in men](https://odinhealthlab.ca/weight-loss-drugs-and-testosterone): what meta-analyses show about semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide and testosterone in men with overweight or obesity, SHBG and free T, protecting muscle during weight loss, and labs to track before and during treatment (Canada and USA).
- [Peptides for men in Canada and the USA](https://odinhealthlab.ca/peptides-canada-usa): Health Canada April 2026 advisory on unauthorized injectable peptides, FDA 503A/503B compounding rules and safety-risk lists, quality risks of research-labelled products, and how Odin helps with labs and plans (does not prescribe peptides).

## Tools
- [Testosterone calculator: unit converter and free T calculator](https://odinhealthlab.ca/testosterone-calculator): converts total testosterone between ng/dL (USA) and nmol/L (Canada) as you type (1 nmol/L = 28.84 ng/dL, from testosterone's molecular weight of 288.4 g/mol) and free testosterone between pg/mL and pmol/L (1 pg/mL = 3.467 pmol/L); calculates free testosterone, percent free and bioavailable testosterone from total T, SHBG and albumin (default 43 g/L) with the Vermeulen equation (JCEM 1999; matches the ISSAM worked example: 10 nmol/L total, SHBG 40, albumin 4.3 g/dL gives about 174 pmol/L free, 1.74 percent); shows in plain words where a result sits against the Endocrine Society harmonized range (264 to 916 ng/dL, 9.2 to 31.8 nmol/L), the AUA 300 ng/dL (about 10.4 nmol/L) and CUA 10 nmol/L thresholds, the EMAS free T cut-off (220 pmol/L, 64 pg/mL) and Canadian lab ranges (Alberta Precision Laboratories 8.0 to 35.0 nmol/L, LifeLabs 8.4 to 28.8 nmol/L); explains why Canada reports SI units (since the early 1980s) and the USA conventional units; and how Odin telehealth puts results from both countries into one unit and builds a plan (Canada and USA).
